analysis.investment_thesis: Bikaji is a good consumer brand growing at ~20% CAGR, but at an EV/EBITDA of 44x the earnings yield is approximately 2.3% — catastrophically below the 6% floor the Magic Formula demands. You are paying a venture-capital multiple for a packaged foods business with only 9.4% operating margins.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 19.5% over 5 years with consistent OCF generation (5/5 positive years)
ROCE of 18.2% is decent and expanding — the business earns above its cost of capital
Strong promoter holding at 73.9% and ethnic snacks brand with distribution reach
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~2.3% (Operating Income INR 330 Cr ÷ EV ~INR 16,756 Cr) means you overpay massively for every rupee of earnings
Operating margin of 9.4% is thin for a consumer brand and vulnerable to raw material inflation (edible oils, pulses)
Capex averaging INR 113 Cr/year consumes >50% of net profit, limiting FCF quality
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 44.17x — earnings yield of barely 2.3% is a Magic Formula disqualifier
Net profit dropped from INR 263 Cr to INR 194 Cr in FY2025 despite revenue growth — margin compression is evident
Debt jumped from INR 166 Cr to INR 310 Cr in FY2025 — unusual for a 'capital-light' consumer company
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bikaji is a well-run ethnic snacks company benefiting from premiumisation trends and expanding distribution in India. But Greenblatt's Magic Formula is ruthlessly quantitative: at a P/E of 66x and EV/EBITDA of 44x, the earnings yield is ~2.3%, and no growth rate justifies that entry price by the formula's logic. ROCE of 18.2% is decent but not the 25%+ that would offset the valuation premium — and margins compressed (net profit fell INR 69 Cr despite revenue growth) suggesting cost pressures are real.

FCF of INR 72 Cr on a market cap of INR 16,550 Cr implies a FCF yield of 0.4% — this stock would rank in the bottom decile of any Magic Formula screen globally. Forward P/E of 49x suggests even optimistic consensus growth bakes in no margin of safety. A great business at a terrible price is still a terrible investment by the Magic Formula.
